title: Heterogeneous model mixworkload orchestrator with fidelity sampler and cost-attribution reporter
author: Ethan Cole
description: Motivation: benchmarking single-model synthetic workloads misses interactions that appear when live traffic mixes multiple model variants (quantized, fp16, small vs large). This PR adds a lightweight orchestrator to run heterogeneous model mix workloads, a fidelity-based sampler to reduce expensive full-profiling runs, and a cost-attribution reporter that slices latency/cost by model mix and sequence-length quantiles. Goals: 1) enable reproducible cross-model mix runs for perf/regression testing, 2) provide a sampling strategy so nightly full-model profiling remains affordable, 3) produce actionable reports for routing/batching policy tuning. Implementation notes: a new CLI 'mixrunner' composes scenarios from YAML workload manifests (models, proportions, seqlen distributions, prefix cache settings), runs them against a local or remote endpoint with concurrent worker pools, and emits structured traces to the existing reporting pipeline. The fidelity sampler implements stratified sampling across (model, seqlen-quantile) with configurable budget and guaranteed coverage for tail quantiles. The reporter produces CSV + JSON summaries with cost attribution (GPU seconds token-weighted) and quantile-sliced latency histograms. Backwards compatibility: workload manifests are optional; existing single-model runners continue to work. Checklist: - [x] CLI and manifest schema - [x] orchestrator loop + concurrency controls - [x] fidelity sampler + unit tests - [x] cost-attribution reporter + CSV/JSON output - [x] integrate with pipeline/CI artifact upload - [x] docs: quickstart + example manifests Related: Linear ENG-3214 (mixworkload orchestration), ENG-3279 (sampling budget heuristics). Links: docs/benchmark-lab/mixrunner.md, benchmark-lab/examples/multi-model-scenarios.yaml

release_notes: Add mixrunner: a heterogeneous model mix workload orchestrator with a fidelity-based sampler to reduce profiling cost and a cost-attribution reporter that emits quantile-sliced latency/cost summaries. Useful for nightly cross-model regression tests and routing policy tuning.
review_comments: Marta Ivanov (review): Nice end-to-end. Two requests: make the default sampler budget conservative for CI and add a flag to force full coverage during release runs.
Ethan Cole (reply): Addressed both; added --force-full-coverage and reduced CI default to 20 samples per (model,quantile) (see sampler.go).
Lucas Park (review): micro-nit on manifest schema: proportions should validate to sum<=1 and allow explicit 'remainder: auto' entry. Also suggest emitting GPU-second estimates in the CSV.
Ethan Cole (reply): Added validation and 'remainder: auto' support; reporter now includes GPU-second estimates and a derived cost column. Added tests.
high_level_summary: Enables realistic mixed-model performance runs with an efficient sampling strategy and produces actionable cost/latency reports for tuning inference routing and batching policies.
testing_notes: Sampler unit tests cover zero-budget, tiny-budget, and full-coverage modes. CI runs a smoke mixed scenario against a local dev endpoint; full nightly pipeline uses a larger cloud endpoint.
